Heh. This article is pretty funny with how it pokes fun critiquing a lack luster SCP article. What really got me was the line "Dr. ████: WHAT THE FUCK IS A DOWNVOTE?!!!" It also struck me, that particular line would be a good means of introducing an inline link to the Standard Form For Downvotes, another joke article that hits a similar comedic cord as 1212-J. As such, I am recommending the following edits:

Changing this:

Dr. ████: WHAT THE FUCK IS A DOWNVOTE?!!!

To this:

Dr. ████: WHAT THE FUCK IS A DOWNVOTE?!!!

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.content:encoded:
Using a question mark with an exclamation point will kill an article for me every single time.

And I'm pretty sure a cousin of this form of meta has been done at least three times as a -j. It might not be the exact same joke, but it's still 'Scientists acting like the Foundation is a wiki in-universe,' if done a bit more bluntly; not necessarily bad in it's directness, but it didn't do it for me. There was a little humor in the juxtaposition of the writing-critique researchers' nonchalant attitude about the breach and the incredulous interviewer, but that's only funny once, and even then it's amusing at best.

In all, it's just not that good, or clever, and nothing else really got me.

And I know I'm not the only one who doesn't take punctuation-abuse seriously. "Guys, look at how incredulous this character is! He's so flummoxed and simultaneously distressed from confusion that it takes multiple punctuation points to express his disdain! DO YOU UNDERSTAND THE DEGREE TO WHICH HE'S UPSET?! SURELY YOU UNDERSTAND THAT THIS IS NOT A NORMAL COMPILATION OF EMOTION?!?!??!??!?!??!?!??!?!" Or at least that's what I see. It's annoying.

Stuff in all caps doesn't bother me so much.
